_meta.purpose: Multi-hop / cross-source retrieval eval — the LEAK-FREE ruler (Cycle 2, Track A.1). Each query leads with the shared BRIDGE tag (so BOTH expected cards enter the tag-path candidate pool) plus one ANCHOR-distinctive tag (so the anchor ranks higher). The 2nd expected card (BRIDGE, expect[1]) is reachable ONLY via that shared bridge tag — it shares NO other query vocabulary, so a content/vector retriever cannot trivially find it. This redesign kills the cycle-1 leakage flaw (the v1 set named both cards' tokens).

format.q: '<bridge-tag> <anchor-distinctive-tag>: <anchor-specific defect in the anchor's own words> — what other <bridge-tag> finding is logged'. The leading tags guarantee both cards are tag-matchable; the anchor-distinctive tag ranks the anchor; the bridge card matches only the bridge tag.
format.anchor: expect[0] — the card the query is written in (findable by multi-tag content match, single-hop).
format.bridge: expect[1] — the card reachable ONLY via the shared bridge tag (the multi-hop edge).
format.bridgeTag: the shared concept tag that connects anchor<->bridge (the multi-hop edge under test). Must be dot-free (queryToTokens strips dots) and carried by BOTH cards.
format.why: 1-line rationale: anchor named by content+distinctive tag, bridge only by the bridge tag.

_meta.leakGate: scripts/multi-hop-eval-leakcheck.mjs computes per-query overlap(query-tokens, bridge-card-tokens)/|query-tokens|. PASS requires bridge-overlap < 0.30 for EVERY query AND anchor-overlap >= 0.30 (valid single-hop seed). Run: node scripts/multi-hop-eval-leakcheck.mjs
_meta.designNotes: v3 fixes two v2 defects: (1) queries now LEAD with the bridge tag so the deterministic tag-path (retrieveRecords, first-10 query tokens, no stopword removal) can actually match both cards — v2's verbose queries pushed the bridge tag past the 10-token cutoff, producing artifactual null,null ranks; (2) dropped the seed<->auto seedvr2 pair (the auto-memory card does NOT carry the seedvr2 tag → unbridgeable) and the run.py-cli pair (dots are stripped by the tokenizer → tag unmatchable). Pairs were ranked by a card-Jaccard scorer (scripts/_pair-scorer.mjs); all pairs carry Jaccard <= 0.12. seed<->workflow dominates because that is where genuine same-concept low-overlap edges live (auto/hermes cards use their own tag space).
_meta.sourceCoverage: 14 seed<->workflow + 2 workflow<->workflow cross-provenance pairs. Hermes (pi-memory-*) does not share concept tags with seed/workflow cards.

baseline.replaced: cycle-1 numbers (setRecall@4=0.567, fullRecall@4=0.333) rode on the LEAKED v1 set and are INVALID.
baseline.gateMetric: fullRecall@4 (strict multi-hop success rate). Baseline 0.375; a lever must reach >= 0.475 (+0.10) to ship. fullRecall@8 (0.563) tracked as the operational/RAG-context metric.
baseline.rerankVerdict: RETIRED — structurally negative on a leak-free eval (Δ setRecall@4 = -0.031). Content-rerank buries the bridge card, which is leak-free precisely because it lacks query vocabulary. Only STRUCTURAL signals (graph/link expansion, entities) can surface it.
baseline.bridgeDiagnostic: bridgeLift is POSITIVE and steep (+0.094, +0.063). Bridge cards are IN the candidate pool (ranked 6-31) but UNDER-RANKED — they share only 1 tag (the bridge tag) with the query while cluster siblings share more. This is a ranking/expansion gap, not a recall gap. The structural lever (link/entity expansion from the anchor) is the bet.
